mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 8% signals a deepening recession, which reduces corporate earnings and increases risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered recession episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for four consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which depresses consumer demand and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >1% MoM for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a period of negative GDP growth (proxied by GDPC1 YoY decline) signals a deep monetary easing in a recession, which supports risk assets and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market gains over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA by >10% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) in at least 55% of triggered housing recovery periods.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals accelerating labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 1% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over three months signals improving demand fundamentals, which expands corporate earnings and reduces risk premia, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises YoY and UNRATE falls >0.5pp over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered early-cycle episodes.
